name: Information Ordering
definition: The ability to arrange things or actions in a certain order or pattern according to a specific rule or set of rules (e.g., patterns of numbers, letters, words, pictures, mathematical operations).

benchmark.name: ARC
benchmark.model_or_system: icecuber (Johan Sokrates Wind): search over a hand-written domain-specific language of grid-transformation programs
benchmark.metric: percent of the 100 hidden test tasks solved (up to 3 guesses allowed per test output; score = 100 x (1 - top-3 error))
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce: typical adults who infer and apply visual or sequential rules in everyday work, such as pattern completion and ordering items by rule

benchmark.name: ARC
benchmark.model_or_system: icecuber (Johan Sokrates Wind), a program search over a hand-built library of 142 grid operations (DSL)
benchmark.metric: percent of hidden test tasks solved (top-3 accuracy; equals 100 minus the leaderboard top-3 error times 100)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population, meaning ordinary adults who infer and apply rules to novel visual patterns. No specialist training is required.

benchmark.name: word_sorting
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce: people who alphabetize or order items by an explicit rule in clerical, filing or data-handling work.

benchmark.name: ARC
benchmark.model_or_system: Team SM (Somayyeh Gholami & Mehran Kazeminia) and Team MindsAI (Jack Cole), tied 1st place in ARCathon 2023
benchmark.metric: percent of hidden private test tasks solved (accuracy, top-3 attempts per test input)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population. Information Ordering is a broad cognitive ability used across many occupations, and ARC tasks need no specialist knowledge.

benchmark.name: PlanBench
benchmark.metric: percent of instances solved with a valid plan (accuracy)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult / relevant educated workforce: people who follow explicit procedural rules to sequence actions at work

benchmark.name: Sudoku-Bench
benchmark.metric: percent of challenge_100 puzzles fully solved (weighted average solve rate across grid sizes)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce: typical workers who apply explicit rules to arrange numbers or symbols. They are not sudoku hobbyists or competitive solvers.

benchmark.name: BIG-Bench Extra Hard
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%), shown on a 0-1 scale as 0.744
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: college-educated adults who routinely sequence and order information by rules at work (analysts, clerical and administrative planners, technical staff).
